title: Maximum Annual Salary tiers by Years of Service (25/30/35%)
summary: A new Player Contract's first-Season Salary plus Unlikely Bonuses is capped at a percentage of the Salary Cap that rises with the player's Years of Service.
detail_paraphrase: For a Player Contract signed on or after the CBA's effective date, the first-Season Salary plus Unlikely Bonuses may not exceed the greater of a Years-of-Service-based percentage of the Salary Cap at execution or 105% of the prior Contract's final-Season Salary. The percentage is 25% for players with fewer than 7 Years of Service, 30% for players with at least 7 but fewer than 10 Years of Service, and 35% for players with 10 or more Years of Service.
conditions: Player Contract entered into on or after the effective date of the Agreement
Applies to first Season covered by the Contract
exceptions: 5th Year Eligible Players meeting the Higher Max Criteria may receive up to 30% (see CONTRACT-002)
Designated Veteran Player Contracts may reach 35% for certain 8-9 Year-of-Service players (see CONTRACT-003)
thresholds: 25% (<7 YoS); 30% (7-9 YoS); 35% (10+ YoS); or 105% of prior final-Season Salary, whichever is greater

title: 5th Year Eligible Player higher max (up to 30%)
summary: A player with exactly 4 Years of Service after his contract who meets the Higher Max Criteria may sign with his Prior Team for up to 30% of the Salary Cap.
detail_paraphrase: A player who has 4 Years of Service as of the June 30 following the last Season of his Contract (a 5th Year Eligible Player) is eligible to receive from his Prior Team up to 30% of the Salary Cap in effect at execution if, as of the July 1 following his fourth Season, he met at least one Higher Max Criterion: (A) named All-NBA first, second, or third team or Defensive Player of the Year in the immediately preceding Season or in two of the prior three Seasons; or (B) named NBA MVP in one of the immediately preceding three Seasons.
conditions: Player has 4 Years of Service as of the June 30 following his Contract's last Season
Player signs with his Prior Team
Player met at least one Higher Max Criterion as of July 1 following his fourth Season
applies_to: 5th Year Eligible Players signing with their Prior Team
thresholds: up to 30% of Salary Cap (instead of the standard 25%)

title: Designated Veteran Player Contract (35% for 8-9 YoS)
summary: A player with 8 or 9 Years of Service who stayed with his original team may sign a Designated Veteran Player Contract for up to 35% of the Salary Cap.
detail_paraphrase: A player who has 8 or 9 Years of Service at execution and rendered those Years for the Team with which he first signed a Player Contract (or changed Teams only by trade during his first four Salary Cap Years under contract) is eligible to enter a Designated Veteran Player Contract receiving from his Prior Team up to 35% of the Salary Cap in effect at execution, provided he met at least one Higher Max Criterion at the time the Contract is executed.
conditions: Player has 8 or 9 Years of Service at execution
Player rendered those Years with his original Team (or changed Teams only by trade in first four Salary Cap Years)
Player met at least one Higher Max Criterion at execution
Signed with the Prior Team
applies_to: players with 8-9 Years of Service eligible as Designated Veterans
thresholds: up to 35% of Salary Cap (instead of the standard 30% for 7-9 YoS)

title: Maximum Annual Salary on Renegotiations
summary: A Renegotiation's Salary plus Unlikely Bonuses in the Renegotiation Season is capped using the same Years-of-Service percentage tiers as new contracts.
detail_paraphrase: No Renegotiation may provide for Salary plus Unlikely Bonuses in the Renegotiation Season exceeding the greater of a Years-of-Service-based percentage of the Salary Cap at execution or 105% of the Salary for the Season prior to the Renegotiation Season. The percentages are 25% (<7 YoS), 30% (7-9 YoS), and 35% (10+ YoS).
conditions: A Renegotiation is being executed
thresholds: 25% / 30% / 35% of Salary Cap by YoS, or 105% of prior-Season Salary, whichever greater

title: Maximum Annual Salary on Extensions (extended-term first Season)
summary: An Extension's first extended-Season Salary plus Unlikely Bonuses is tested against the Years-of-Service max tiers on July 1 and auto-reduced if it exceeds them.
detail_paraphrase: For any Extension whose extended term begins on or after the effective date, if on July 1 of the Salary Cap Year encompassing the first extended Season the Salary plus Unlikely Bonuses exceed the applicable max (25%/30%/35% of the Salary Cap, or 105% of the original Contract's final-Season Salary, whichever greater), the amount is deemed amended down to the maximum. Reductions are applied first to any signing bonus allocated to the first extended Salary Cap Year, then to Likely and Unlikely Bonuses pro rata, then to Base Compensation, with later-year signing-bonus allocations reduced proportionately. A 5th Year Eligible Player who signed a Rookie Scale Extension may receive a negotiated 25%-30% if he met a Higher Max Criterion; a Designated Veteran Player Extension may reach 30%-35% for qualifying 7-8 YoS players.
conditions: Extension whose extended term begins on or after the effective date
Tested on July 1 of the Salary Cap Year of the first extended Season
exceptions: Rookie Scale Extension 5th Year Eligible Player negotiated 25-30% with Higher Max Criteria
Designated Veteran Player Extension negotiated 30-35% for 7-8 YoS qualifying players
applies_to: players signing veteran or rookie-scale extensions
thresholds: 25% / 30% / 35% of Salary Cap by YoS, or 105% of original final-Season Salary

title: 5th Year Eligible Player 30% deal requires 4+ Season length
summary: Any contract or Rookie Scale Extension giving a 5th Year Eligible Player more than 25% of the cap must be at least four Seasons long.
detail_paraphrase: Any Contract or Rookie Scale Extension between a 5th Year Eligible Player and a Team that provides first-Season Salary plus Unlikely Bonuses greater than 25% of the Salary Cap (i.e., reaching the 30% higher max) must be for at least four Seasons, excluding any Option Year and, for a Rookie Scale Extension, excluding the final Season of the player's Rookie Scale Contract.
conditions: 5th Year Eligible Player
First-Season Salary plus Unlikely Bonuses greater than 25% of the Salary Cap
applies_to: 5th Year Eligible Players receiving above-25% maxes
thresholds: minimum 4 Seasons (excluding Option Year)

title: Minimum Player Salary floor
summary: Except for specified short/two-way contracts, no Player Contract may pay less than the applicable Minimum Annual Salary Scale amount.
detail_paraphrase: Other than 10-Day, Rest-of-Season, and Two-Way Contracts, no Player Contract may provide a Salary below the applicable scale amount in the Minimum Annual Salary Scale for that Salary Cap Year. The applicable scale is fixed by the Salary Cap Year encompassing the first Season of the Contract and applies for every Season of the Contract.
conditions: Standard Player Contract (not 10-Day, Rest-of-Season, or Two-Way)
exceptions: 10-Day Contracts (Section 9)
Rest-of-Season Contracts (Section 10)
Two-Way Contracts (Section 11)
thresholds: no less than applicable Minimum Annual Salary Scale amount

title: Minimum salary scale by Years of Service (Exhibit C)
summary: The baseline Minimum Annual Salary Scale sets a minimum for each Years-of-Service level, ranging from $1,017,781 at 0 YoS to $2,905,851+ at 10+ YoS.
detail_paraphrase: The Baseline Minimum Annual Salary Scale lists minimum salaries indexed by Years of Service. Baseline Year 1 amounts include $1,017,781 (0 YoS), $1,637,966 (1 YoS), $1,836,090 (2 YoS), $1,902,133 (3 YoS), $1,968,175 (4 YoS), $2,133,278 (5 YoS), $2,298,385 (6 YoS), $2,463,490 (7 YoS), $2,628,597 (8 YoS), $2,641,682 (9 YoS), and $2,905,851 (10+ YoS). The scale also provides multi-year columns. These are baseline figures subject to annual escalation under the Agreement.
conditions: Minimum determined by the player's Years of Service
applies_to: all players paid at the minimum
thresholds: Baseline Year 1: $1,017,781 (0 YoS) up to $2,905,851 (10+ YoS)
notes: Figures are labeled 'Baseline' — the actual minimum each Salary Cap Year is the baseline escalated per the Agreement, so dollar amounts should be treated as baseline values, not the live-season minimums.

title: Minimum salary auto-amendment each July 1
summary: Each July 1 any non-Two-Way contract paying below the new applicable minimum is deemed amended up to the applicable Minimum Player Salary.
detail_paraphrase: On July 1 of each Salary Cap Year, any Player Contract other than a Two-Way Contract that provides an upcoming-Season Salary below the applicable Minimum Player Salary (based on the Minimum Annual Salary Scale applicable to that Contract) is automatically deemed amended to provide that applicable Minimum Player Salary.
conditions: Contract is not a Two-Way Contract
Upcoming-Season Salary is below the applicable Minimum Player Salary
exceptions: Two-Way Contracts
applies_to: existing contracts below the minimum at season rollover
thresholds: raised to applicable Minimum Player Salary

title: Annual raise/decrease limit 5% (non-Bird)
summary: For contracts other than Qualifying/Early Qualifying Veteran Free Agents re-signing with their Prior Team, Salary may change year to year by at most 5% of the first-year Salary.
detail_paraphrase: For each Salary Cap Year after the first, a player's Salary (excluding Incentive Compensation) and his Regular Salary may each increase or decrease relative to the prior year by no more than 5% of the first Salary Cap Year's corresponding amount. If the first year includes Incentive Compensation, each bonus may increase or decrease in later years by up to 5% of its first-year amount. This 5% rule applies to all contracts except those between Qualifying or Early Qualifying Veteran Free Agents and their Prior Team.
conditions: Contract is not between a Qualifying/Early Qualifying Veteran Free Agent and his Prior Team
exceptions: Qualifying/Early Qualifying Veteran Free Agents re-signing with Prior Team use 8% (see CONTRACT-011)
Two-Way Contracts excluded (governed by Art II Sec 11(a))
applies_to: contracts signed with Room or exceptions other than with Prior Team
thresholds: +/- 5% of first-year Salary per year

title: Annual raise/decrease limit 8% (Bird/Early Bird re-signing)
summary: Contracts between Qualifying or Early Qualifying Veteran Free Agents and their Prior Team allow up to 8% annual raises/decreases off the first-year amount.
detail_paraphrase: For contracts between Qualifying Veteran Free Agents or Early Qualifying Veteran Free Agents and their Prior Team, each Salary Cap Year after the first may change the player's Salary (excluding Incentive Compensation) and Regular Salary by up to 8% of the first-year corresponding amount, and each first-year bonus may change by up to 8% of its first-year amount. This does not apply to certain exception-based signings listed in Section 6 (which revert to the 5% rule).
conditions: Contract between a Qualifying or Early Qualifying Veteran Free Agent and his Prior Team
exceptions: Contracts signed pursuant to Sections 6(d)(4), 6(e)(4), 6(f)(3), 6(g)(4), or 8(e)(1) revert to the 5% rule (CONTRACT-010)
applies_to: Bird and Early Bird free agents re-signing with their Prior Team
thresholds: +/- 8% of first-year Salary per year

title: Annual raise/decrease limit on Extensions (8%)
summary: Extensions (other than trade-related Section 8(e)(2) extensions) allow up to 8% annual raises/decreases off the first extended-term year.
detail_paraphrase: For each Salary Cap Year after the first year of the extended term, an Extension may change the player's Salary (excluding Incentive Compensation) and Regular Salary by up to 8% of the first extended-year corresponding amount, and each first-extended-year bonus by up to 8% of its first-extended-year amount. This rule covers all Extensions except those entered in connection with a trade under Section 8(e)(2).
conditions: Extension not entered in connection with a Section 8(e)(2) trade
exceptions: Section 8(e)(2) trade extensions use 5% (see CONTRACT-013)
thresholds: +/- 8% of first extended-year Salary per year

title: Annual raise/decrease limit on trade-extensions (5%)
summary: Extensions signed in connection with a trade under Section 8(e)(2) are limited to 5% annual raises/decreases off the first extended-term year.
detail_paraphrase: For Extensions entered into in connection with a trade pursuant to Section 8(e)(2), each Salary Cap Year after the first extended-term year may change the player's Salary (excluding Incentive Compensation) and Regular Salary by no more than 5% of the first extended-year amount, and each first-extended-year bonus by up to 5% of its first-extended-year amount.
conditions: Extension entered into in connection with a Section 8(e)(2) trade
thresholds: +/- 5% of first extended-year Salary per year

title: Maximum contract length by signing type
summary: Standard contracts run up to 4 Seasons; Bird re-signings up to 5; rookie-scale extensions up to 6; veteran extensions up to 5; Designated Veteran Player Extensions exactly 6.
detail_paraphrase: Unless a shorter term is specified elsewhere, a Player Contract signed after the effective date may cover at most 4 Seasons from signing. A Contract between a Qualifying Veteran Free Agent and his Prior Team may cover up to 5 Seasons. A Rookie Scale Extension may cover, in the aggregate, up to 6 Seasons from signing. A Veteran Extension under Article VII Section 7(a) (other than a Designated Veteran Player Extension) may cover up to 5 Seasons. A Designated Veteran Player Extension must cover exactly 6 Seasons. All these maximums are inclusive of any Option Year.
conditions: Contract entered after the effective date
exceptions: Two-Way Contracts limited to 2 Seasons (see CONTRACT-031)
10-Day and Rest-of-Season Contracts are short-term
thresholds: 4 (standard) / 5 (Bird re-sign) / 6 (rookie-scale ext.) / 5 (veteran ext.) / 6 (Designated Vet ext., exactly)

title: Computation of contract length (partial season counts as one)
summary: A contract or extension signed mid-Season counts that Season as a full Season for length purposes.
detail_paraphrase: For computing maximum length, if a Contract or Extension is signed after a Season begins, the Season of signing counts as one full Season. For an Extension signed from the end of a Season through the immediately following June 30, the just-completed Season counts as one full Season of the Extension.
conditions: Contract or Extension signed after the start of a Season, or an Extension signed in the post-Season-through-June-30 window
thresholds: signing Season counts as 1 full Season

title: Team Option clause requirements
summary: A team-favorable Option may extend a contract one year only, exercisable once, at no less than 100% of the prior year's pay and otherwise unchanged terms.
detail_paraphrase: Except for Rookie Scale Contract options, a Player Contract may contain a Team Option only if it: is specifically negotiated; extends the Contract no more than one year beyond the stated term; is exercisable only once; provides Option-Year Salary (excluding Incentive Compensation), Likely Bonuses, and Unlikely Bonuses no less than 100% of those in the last stated-term year; and (except for Second Round Pick Exception contracts) keeps all other terms unchanged from the last stated-term year, including the protected percentage of Base Compensation.
conditions: Contract is not a Rookie Scale Contract option
exceptions: Article VIII Section 1 Rookie Scale Contract options (see CONTRACT-028)
Second Round Pick Exception contracts exempt from the 'all other terms unchanged' requirement
thresholds: max 1 Option Year; Option-Year pay >= 100% of last stated-term year

title: Player Option clause requirements
summary: A player-favorable Option may extend a contract one year only, exercisable once, at no less than 100% of the prior year's pay with otherwise unchanged terms.
detail_paraphrase: A Player Contract may contain a Player Option only if it: is specifically negotiated; extends the Contract no more than one year; is exercisable only once; provides Option-Year Salary (excluding Incentive Compensation), Likely Bonuses, and Unlikely Bonuses no less than 100% of the last stated-term year; and keeps all other terms unchanged (including the protected percentage of Base Compensation). If the Player Option Year has Base Compensation protection, Exhibit 2 must include one of two prescribed clauses governing whether protection survives a pre-exercise team termination. A contract using the protection-relieving clause may not make the Player Option exercisable earlier than the day after the team's last game of the Season before the Option Year.
conditions: Player Option included in a Player Contract
thresholds: max 1 Option Year; Option-Year pay >= 100% of last stated-term year

title: Early Termination Option (ETO) requirements
summary: An ETO may be exercised only once and may take effect no earlier than the end of the fourth Season of the contract.
detail_paraphrase: An Early Termination Option may be included only if exercisable once and effective no earlier than the end of the Contract's fourth Season. A Contract without an ETO at signing may not add one during its original term. Entering a veteran Extension (non-rookie-scale) bars adding an ETO and requires eliminating any existing ETO. A Rookie Scale Contract Extension may simultaneously add an ETO if exercisable once and effective no earlier than the end of the fourth Season of the extended term.
conditions: Contract includes or seeks to include an ETO
exceptions: Rookie Scale Extension may add an ETO effective no earlier than end of fourth extended-term Season
applies_to: contracts of five or more Seasons with an ETO
thresholds: exercisable once; effective no earlier than end of 4th Season

title: No conditional options; fixed exercise rights and deadlines
summary: Option/ETO exercise rights must be fixed at signing (no conditions), and Options/ETOs have set June exercise deadlines.
detail_paraphrase: If a Contract contains any Option or ETO, the exercise right must be fixed at signing and cannot be contingent on any individually negotiated condition (and an ETO's Effective Season must also be fixed). An ETO must be exercised by 5:00 p.m. ET on the June 29 immediately before its Effective Season. An Option must be exercised by 5:00 p.m. ET on the June 29 before the Option Season, except that an Option in favor of a player who would become a Restricted Free Agent if not exercised must be exercised before the June 25 immediately prior to the Option Season.
conditions: Contract contains an Option or ETO
applies_to: all contracts containing options or ETOs
thresholds: ETO deadline June 29 5pm ET; Option deadline June 29 (or June 25 if non-exercise would create RFA)
notes: Section 3 (no conditional options, p.338) and Section 4 (exercise period, p.338) combined into one rule covering option exercise mechanics.

title: Veteran Extension eligibility and timing
summary: Only 3+ Season contracts may be extended, and only after the second (3-4 Season) or third (5-6 Season) anniversary of signing.
detail_paraphrase: No non-rookie-scale Player Contract may be extended except as follows: a Contract of 3 or 4 Seasons (including any Option Year) may be extended no sooner than the second anniversary of signing; a Contract of 5 or 6 Seasons may be extended no sooner than the third anniversary; and a Contract of 1 or 2 Seasons may not be extended at all. Designated Veteran Player Extensions require the third anniversary and off-season execution. A Contract whose term was shortened by a player's ETO exercise may not be extended. A player who will not be a Qualifying Veteran Free Agent at the conclusion of his Contract is not eligible to extend under Section 7(a).
conditions: Contract is not a Rookie Scale Contract
Player will be a Qualifying Veteran Free Agent at the Contract's conclusion
exceptions: 1-2 Season contracts cannot be extended
Contracts shortened by ETO exercise cannot be extended
thresholds: 2nd anniversary (3-4 Seasons) / 3rd anniversary (5-6 Seasons); 1-2 Season contracts ineligible

title: Veteran Extension salary terms (140% / Estimated Average)
summary: A non-designated veteran extension's first extended-year salary may be up to the greater of 140% of the prior final-year Regular Salary or 140% of the Estimated Average Player Salary.
detail_paraphrase: A non-designated veteran Extension may provide first-extended-year Salary (excluding Incentive Compensation) up to the greater of 140% of the original Contract's last-year Regular Salary or 140% of the Estimated Average Player Salary for the Salary Cap Year the Extension is signed (reduced by any first-extended-year Incentive Compensation). If the original last year had Incentive Compensation, first-extended-year Likely and Unlikely Bonuses may be up to 140% of those amounts. A Designated Veteran Player Extension instead may reach the Article II Section 7 maximum. Trade-related Section 8(e)(2) extensions use 105% (pre-2024-25) or the greater of 120% / 120% of Estimated Average Player Salary (on/after 2024-25). A 10+ Season same-team player whose final original year declined in Salary may instead use 107.5% of the greater of the original-term Regular Salary average or the final-year Regular Salary.
conditions: Veteran Extension under Section 7(a)
exceptions: Designated Veteran Player Extensions use Article II Section 7 max
Section 8(e)(2) trade extensions use 105% or 120%/120% of Estimated Average
10+ Season same-team declining-salary players may use 107.5% formula
thresholds: greater of 140% of prior final-year Regular Salary or 140% of Estimated Average Player Salary

title: Rookie Scale Extension eligibility, timing, and salary
summary: A First Round Pick may extend his Rookie Scale Contract in a defined window; the first extended-year salary may reach the Article II Section 7 maximum.
detail_paraphrase: A First Round Pick may extend his Rookie Scale Contract during the window from 12:01 p.m. ET on the last day of the Moratorium Period through 6:00 p.m. ET on the day before the first Regular Season day of the second Option Year (assuming the Team exercised that Option). The first extended-year Salary plus Unlikely Bonuses may total up to the Article II Section 7 maximum, with annual increases/decreases under the 8% extension rule. A player who will not be a Qualifying Veteran Free Agent at his Rookie Scale Contract's conclusion is ineligible to extend.
conditions: Player is a First Round Pick on a Rookie Scale Contract
Player will be a Qualifying Veteran Free Agent at the Contract's conclusion
Within the prescribed extension window
applies_to: First Round Picks extending rookie-scale contracts
thresholds: first extended-year Salary plus Unlikely Bonuses up to Article II Section 7 max

title: Rookie Scale Extension max-percentage criteria
summary: A Rookie Scale Extension may peg the first extended-year salary to the Maximum Annual Salary, or to negotiated 25-30% cap percentages tied to Higher Max Criteria.
detail_paraphrase: A Rookie Scale Extension may set the first-extended-year Salary at the player's Maximum Annual Salary, or use cap-percentage language. If the First Round Pick already met a Higher Max Criterion at execution, the parties may agree on 25%-30% of the Salary Cap. Otherwise the Extension may provide 25%, escalating to a negotiated 25%-30% if the player meets a Higher Max Criterion during the fourth Rookie Scale Season; alternatively, tiered percentages may be specified (e.g., 27% for All-NBA Second Team, 28% for All-NBA First Team, 30% for NBA MVP). Such Extensions may not include Incentive Compensation and are deemed amended on July 1 to specific Salaries based on the applicable Maximum Annual Salary.
conditions: Rookie Scale Extension for a First Round Pick
applies_to: First Round Picks signing max rookie-scale extensions
thresholds: 25%-30% of Salary Cap (27%/28%/30% tiered examples for All-NBA 2nd/1st/MVP)

title: Designated Veteran Player Extension salary terms
summary: A Designated Veteran Player Extension may set the first extended-year salary at a negotiated 30%-35% of the Salary Cap.
detail_paraphrase: A Designated Veteran Player Extension may set the first-extended-year Salary at a negotiated percentage of the Salary Cap that is no less than 30% and no greater than 35%. Later-year Salaries may be adjusted within Article VII Section 5(a) limits. The Extension is deemed amended on July 1 to specific Salaries based on the applicable Maximum Annual Salary and may not include Incentive Compensation.
conditions: Designated Veteran Player Extension is being executed
thresholds: 30%-35% of Salary Cap (negotiated)

title: Rookie Scale Contract structure for First Round Picks
summary: A First Round Pick's Rookie Scale Contract is 2 guaranteed Seasons plus two consecutive team Option Years (third and fourth Seasons).
detail_paraphrase: Each Rookie Scale Contract covers two Seasons plus a team Option for the third Season and a second team Option for the fourth Season. The third-Season Option is exercisable from the day after the first Season's last day through the following October 31; the fourth-Season Option from the day after the second Season's last day through the following October 31 (deadlines roll to the next business day if October 31 is a weekend/Federal Holiday). The applicable Rookie Salary Scale is fixed by the first Season covered, and the player's Rookie Scale Amounts are set by his draft selection number. An unsigned First Round Pick's applicable Rookie Scale Amount is reduced daily from January 10 through the Regular Season's end.
conditions: Player is a First Round Pick signing a Rookie Scale Contract
thresholds: 2 Seasons + 2 team Option Years; Option deadlines October 31

title: Baseline Rookie Salary Scale amounts (Exhibit B)
summary: The Baseline Rookie Salary Scale lists first/second/third-year salaries by draft pick, from $9.21M (pick 1, 1st year) down to $1.83M (pick 30, 1st year).
detail_paraphrase: Exhibit B provides baseline Rookie Scale Amounts by first-round selection number, including first-year, second-year, and third-year (first Option) salaries, the fourth-year (second Option) percentage increase, and the Qualifying Offer percentage increase. For example, pick 1 is $9,212,600 / $9,673,400 / $10,134,000 with a 26.1% fourth-year increase and 40.0% qualifying-offer increase; pick 30 is $1,828,300 / $1,919,600 / $2,011,300 with an 80.5% fourth-year increase and 60.0% qualifying-offer increase. These are baseline figures (in $000's) subject to annual adjustment.
conditions: Amount determined by the player's draft selection number
applies_to: First Round Picks by draft position
notes: Figures labeled 'Baseline' — the live Rookie Salary Scale each Salary Cap Year is the baseline escalated per the Agreement, so treat dollar amounts as baseline, not live-season values.

title: Rookie Scale Contract compensation bounds (80%-120%)
summary: A Rookie Scale Contract must pay at least 80% and at most 120% of the applicable Rookie Scale Amount, with no signing bonus.
detail_paraphrase: In each of the two covered Seasons and the first Option Year, a Rookie Scale Contract must provide Current Base Compensation of at least the greater of 80% of the applicable Rookie Scale Amount or the player's applicable Minimum Player Salary. Salary plus Unlikely Bonuses may not exceed 120% of the applicable Rookie Scale Amount in any Salary Cap Year, and the Contract may not include a signing bonus (except a qualifying international-player payment) or a loan. The Contract must guarantee lack-of-skill and injury-or-illness protection of at least 80% of the applicable Rookie Scale Amount in each of the first two Seasons and the first Option Year.
conditions: Rookie Scale Contract for a First Round Pick
exceptions: International-player payment in excess of the Excluded International Player Payment Amount is permitted
applies_to: First Round Picks on rookie-scale contracts
thresholds: 80% floor (Base Comp / protection); 120% ceiling (Salary plus Unlikely Bonuses)

title: Rookie Scale second Option Year terms locked to first
summary: A Rookie Scale Contract's second Option Year keeps all first-Option-Year terms except Salary, which increases by the scale's specified percentage.
detail_paraphrase: The terms and conditions of the second Option Year of a Rookie Scale Contract (other than the Base Compensation payment schedule) are unchanged from the first Option Year, including the protected Base Compensation percentage, except that the Salary (excluding Incentive Compensation), and each bonus if Incentive Compensation was provided, increases over the first Option Year by the percentage specified in the applicable Rookie Salary Scale.
conditions: Rookie Scale Contract with both Option Years
applies_to: First Round Picks entering their fourth Season option
thresholds: second Option Year Salary increased by scale-specified percentage

title: Later-signed First Round Pick contract options
summary: A First Round Pick who waits three Seasons may sign a standard Rookie Scale Contract or, with Room, a 3+ Season deal above 120% of the first-year scale amount.
detail_paraphrase: A First Round Pick who does not sign with his rights-holding Team for any of the three Seasons after his draft (and did not play intercollegiate basketball in that period) may either sign a standard Rookie Scale Contract or, if the Team has Room above the applicable first-year Rookie Scale Amount, sign a Contract of at least three Seasons (excluding any Option Year) with first-Season Base Compensation greater than 120% of the applicable first-year Rookie Scale Amount.
conditions: First Round Pick did not sign with rights-holding Team for three Seasons post-draft
Did not play intercollegiate basketball during that period
exceptions: Loss-of-draft-rights situations under Section 3 (see CONTRACT-030)
thresholds: alternative: 3+ Seasons, first-year Base Comp > 120% of first-year scale amount

title: Loss of First Round Pick draft rights
summary: If a Team fails to tender, withdraws a tender, or renounces a First Round Pick (or a Subsequent-Draft pick goes unsigned a year), the player becomes a Rookie Free Agent.
detail_paraphrase: If a Team fails to make, withdraws, or renounces a Required Tender to a First Round Pick under Article X, or a Subsequent-Draft First Round Pick goes unsigned for a year, the Rookie Scale rules of Sections 1 and 2 cease to apply and the player becomes a Rookie Free Agent. That Team is then barred from signing the player until he has first signed with another NBA Team and either completes that contract's services or has it terminated via the NBA waiver procedure.
conditions: Team fails to tender, withdraws tender, or renounces a First Round Pick, or a Subsequent-Draft pick goes unsigned for one year
applies_to: First Round Picks who lose rookie-scale status

title: Two-Way Contract salary, term, and eligibility
summary: A Two-Way Player Salary is 50% of the 0-YoS minimum (pro-rated); the term may not exceed 2 Seasons and excludes options.
detail_paraphrase: A Two-Way Contract pays a Two-Way Player Salary equal to 50% of the 0-Years-of-Service Minimum Annual Salary, pro-rated by days remaining in the Regular Season when signed. It may include no bonuses, Incentive Compensation, deferred compensation, or loans. Its term may not exceed two Seasons and may not contain any Option Year or ETO. No Team may sign a player to a Two-Way Contract after March 4, sign/convert a player who has or may reach 4+ Years of Service during the Contract (with a narrow one-Season exception), or arrange for a player to be under Two-Way Contracts spanning more than three Salary Cap Years with the same Team. No Team may roster more than three Two-Way Players.
conditions: Two-Way Contract between a Team and a Two-Way Player
exceptions: A 4-YoS player may sign a one-Season Two-Way Contract if his credited Year was for a Season in which he did not play but stayed rostered all Regular Season
thresholds: Salary = 50% of 0-YoS minimum (pro-rated); term <= 2 Seasons; max 3 per roster; no signings after March 4; 4+ YoS ineligible

title: Standard NBA Contract Conversion Option (Two-Way)
summary: Every Two-Way Contract gives the Team an option to convert it to a minimum-salary Standard NBA Contract for the remaining term.
detail_paraphrase: Every Two-Way Contract must give the Team an option to convert it to a Standard NBA Contract paying the player's applicable Minimum Player Salary for a term equal to the remainder of the original Two-Way term. The Standard NBA Contract Conversion Option may be exercised from July 1 through just before the Team's last Regular Season game in each Salary Cap Year of the Two-Way Contract. On conversion the Contract is no longer governed by Two-Way rules.
conditions: Contract is a Two-Way Contract
applies_to: Teams converting Two-Way Players to standard deals
thresholds: convert to applicable Minimum Player Salary for remaining term

title: Exhibit 10 bonus and Two-Way Conversion Option
summary: An Exhibit 10 adds a $5,000-to-Maximum bonus and a team option to convert a minimum-salary deal to a Two-Way Contract before the Regular Season.
detail_paraphrase: An Exhibit 10 may entitle a waived player to an Exhibit 10 Bonus between $5,000 and the Maximum Exhibit 10 Bonus Amount ($75,000 for 2023-24, escalated by the Salary Cap ratio thereafter) if he timely joins and serves 60 consecutive days with the Team's NBAGL affiliate. Every Exhibit 10 also provides a Two-Way Player Conversion Option exercisable before the first Regular Season day, converting the Contract to a Two-Way Contract and triggering a Conversion Protection Amount ($5,000 to the Maximum, equal to any Exhibit 10 Bonus). A Contract with an Exhibit 10 must be one Season at the Minimum Player Salary with no other bonuses and no Section 3(i) protection (other than via Section 3(s)(ii)). No Team may hold more than six Exhibit 10 contracts at once.
conditions: Contract contains an Exhibit 10
Team has an NBAGL affiliate at execution
thresholds: Exhibit 10 Bonus $5,000-$75,000 (2023-24, escalated); max 6 per Team; 1 Season at minimum
notes: Section 3(s) (Exhibit 10 bonus mechanics, pp.23-24) combined with Section 11(h) conversion mechanics (pp.56-58).

title: 10-Day Contract rules
summary: From January 5, a Team may sign a player to a 10-day (or three-game) minimum-salary contract, at most twice per player per Season.
detail_paraphrase: Beginning January 5 of a Season, a Team may sign a player (not a Two-Way Player) to a 10-Day Contract running the longer of ten days or three Team games, at the Minimum Player Salary. A Team may not sign the same player to more than two 10-Day Contracts in a Season, and the number of concurrent 10-Day Contracts is capped by the size of the Team's Active and Inactive Lists (0 at 12 players, up to 3 at 15). A 10-Day Contract may not extend to or past the Team's last Regular Season game (with a hardship-rule exception). It is terminated by written notice rather than waivers.
conditions: Signed on or after January 5 of a Season
Player is not a Two-Way Player
exceptions: Hardship-rule signings may be 10-Day Contracts at any time and may run to the number of days remaining in the Regular Season
thresholds: longer of 10 days or 3 games; max 2 per player per Season; salary = Minimum Player Salary

title: Rest-of-Season Contract rules
summary: After the first day of the Regular Season, a Team may sign a player to a remainder-of-Season contract at no less than the Minimum Player Salary.
detail_paraphrase: At any time after the first day of an NBA Regular Season, a Team may sign a player to a Rest-of-Season Contract covering the remainder of that Season. Its Salary may not be less than the Minimum Player Salary. Two-Way Contracts are not subject to the Rest-of-Season requirements.
conditions: Signed after the first day of the Regular Season
exceptions: Two-Way Contracts
applies_to: players signed for the remainder of a Season
thresholds: Salary >= Minimum Player Salary

title: Signing bonus caps
summary: Signing bonuses are capped at 15% of compensation (10% for Offer Sheets), and incentive compensation at 20% of Regular Salary.
detail_paraphrase: No Uniform Player Contract may provide Incentive Compensation for a Season exceeding 20% of the Regular Salary for that Season. No signing bonus may exceed 15% of the Contract's Compensation excluding Incentive Compensation (for an Extension, of the extended term). No Offer Sheet signing bonus may exceed 10% of its compensation excluding Incentive Compensation. If a player is suspended for intentionally refusing to render services, the Team may recover a pro-rated portion of the signing bonus based on games suspended.
conditions: Contract provides for a signing bonus and/or Incentive Compensation
applies_to: contracts with signing bonuses or incentives
thresholds: signing bonus <= 15% of comp (10% for Offer Sheets); Incentive Compensation <= 20% of Regular Salary

title: Performance (Unlikely) bonus cap 15%
summary: Unlikely Bonuses in any Salary Cap Year may not exceed 15% of the player's Regular Salary for that year.
detail_paraphrase: No Player Contract may provide Unlikely Bonuses in any Salary Cap Year exceeding 15% of the player's Regular Salary for that year as of signing. For an Extension, if Unlikely Bonuses in the signing year already exceed 15%, the same percentage may carry into the first extended year. No Renegotiation may increase Unlikely Bonuses if doing so would push any year's Unlikely Bonuses above 15% of Regular Salary. A new Unlikely Bonus in the first year may not be set so high that, if treated as Salary, it would put the Team over the Room used to sign the Contract.
conditions: Player Contract provides for Unlikely Bonuses
exceptions: Extensions may carry forward a higher signing-year percentage
thresholds: Unlikely Bonuses <= 15% of Regular Salary per Salary Cap Year

title: No Futures Contracts (current-Season coverage required)
summary: Every contract must cover at least the current/upcoming Season, be consecutive, and may not be signed in the late-season/offseason blackout window.
detail_paraphrase: Every Player Contract must cover at least the then-current Season (or the upcoming Season if signed from July 1 through the day before the Season). No Team and player may enter a Player Contract from the start of the Team's last Regular Season game through the following June 30 (amendments otherwise permitted are not barred). A multi-Season Contract must cover a consecutive period of Seasons. Limited exceptions allow June acceptance of a Required Tender/Qualifying Offer and a February-1-through-June-30 Rookie Scale Contract for certain First Round Picks who were under contract with a non-NBA team.
conditions: Any new Player Contract
exceptions: June acceptance of an outstanding Required Tender or Qualifying Offer
Certain First Round Picks may sign Rookie Scale Contracts Feb 1-June 30 for the following Season
thresholds: must cover current/upcoming Season; no signings from last RS game through June 30

title: Renegotiation eligibility and timing
summary: Only 4+ Season contracts may be renegotiated, no sooner than the third anniversary of signing, and only by under-cap teams (never March 1-June 30).
detail_paraphrase: A Player Contract of four or more Seasons may be renegotiated no sooner than the third anniversary of signing. A Contract renegotiated for a >5% increase, or extended, may not be renegotiated again until the third anniversary of that Extension/Renegotiation. Only a Team with Team Salary below the Salary Cap may renegotiate, and the additional Regular Salary/Likely/Unlikely Bonuses for the Renegotiation Season may not exceed the Team's Room; each increased category must also be increased for remaining Seasons (within 8% annual change limits). No Renegotiation may occur from March 1 through June 30, and a Team at or above the Salary Cap may never renegotiate. A Renegotiation may not contain a signing bonus unless accompanied by an Extension that permits one.
conditions: Contract of four or more Seasons
Third anniversary of signing reached
Team Salary below the Salary Cap
exceptions: No renegotiations March 1-June 30
Teams at/above the Salary Cap may never renegotiate
thresholds: 4+ Seasons; 3rd anniversary; under-cap only; no March 1-June 30 renegotiations

title: No negotiated salary decreases; simultaneous extend-and-renegotiate limit
summary: Teams and players may not negotiate a year-over-year salary decrease; a simultaneous extend-and-renegotiate may drop first extended-year salary by at most 40%.
detail_paraphrase: A Team and player may never negotiate a decrease in Salary or Incentive Compensation for any Salary Cap Year of a Contract. A Contract extended under Section 7(a) may be renegotiated simultaneously only as permitted by the renegotiation rules; in that case the first-extended-year Salary (excluding Incentive Compensation) may decrease by no more than 40% of the player's renegotiated Regular Salary in the original term's last year (with a parallel 40% limit on Likely/Unlikely Bonuses if renegotiated).
conditions: Contract amendment negotiated
exceptions: Simultaneous extend-and-renegotiate allows up to a 40% first-extended-year decrease
thresholds: no salary decreases; max 40% first-extended-year decrease on extend-and-renegotiate

title: Allowable amendments to the Uniform Player Contract
summary: A Uniform Player Contract may be amended only in the specific respects enumerated in Article II Section 3; unauthorized amendments are disapproved and void.
detail_paraphrase: A player and Team may amend a Uniform Player Contract only in the respects listed in Article II Section 3, including: compensation per Season (Exhibit 1); lump-sum and signing bonuses; trade restrictions; compensation protection (Exhibit 2); minimum-salary designations (Exhibit 1A); Two-Way terms (Exhibit 1B); physical-exam conditions (Exhibit 6); Non-Guaranteed Training Camp Contracts (Exhibit 9); and Exhibit 10 NBAGL provisions. Any amendment not specifically permitted, or any unauthorized subsequent amendment, is disapproved by the Commissioner and rendered null and void. Two-Way Contracts and Exhibit 10 contracts may not be extended, renegotiated, or contain an Option Year or ETO.
conditions: A Uniform Player Contract is being amended
exceptions: Amendments expressly permitted under Sections 3, 6, 7(d), 9, 10, 12, Article VII Section 7, or Article XII
notes: Covers the limitation-on-amendments framework (Section 2) and the enumerated allowable amendments (Section 3) at a summary level; individual exhibit mechanics captured in dedicated rules where in scope.

title: Non-Guaranteed Training Camp Contract (Exhibit 9)
summary: An Exhibit 9 lets a one-Season minimum/Two-Way contract eliminate base-comp protection if terminated before the Regular Season, subject to roster and quantity limits.
detail_paraphrase: An Exhibit 9 may eliminate the player's right to Base Compensation if the Contract is terminated before the first day of the Regular Season, but only if: the Contract is one Season, provides the Minimum Player Salary (no bonuses) or Two-Way Salary, and has no Section 3(i) compensation protection (a Non-Guaranteed, Training Camp Contract); at signing the Team has at least 14 players signed to Player Contracts (excluding Two-Way and Non-Guaranteed Training Camp Contracts); and no Team is party to more than six Non-Guaranteed Training Camp Contracts at once.
conditions: Contract is one Season at Minimum Player Salary or Two-Way Salary with no Section 3(i) protection
Team has >= 14 players signed to Player Contracts at signing
Team holds <= 6 such contracts
thresholds: 1 Season; minimum or Two-Way salary; >=14 rostered at signing; max 6 per Team

title: Death-protection and life-insurance limits
summary: Aggregate Base Compensation protected for death is capped at $30,000,000, with structured limits on team-reimbursed life-insurance coverage.
detail_paraphrase: For contracts entered into or extended on or after the effective date, the maximum aggregate Base Compensation that may be protected for death is $30,000,000. A player (with stated exceptions) may purchase term life insurance for which the Team may reimburse premiums, capped by formulas tied to unearned unprotected Base Compensation and an $85,000,000 ceiling, and not exceeding ten-year guaranteed term coverage at preferred rates. If a Contract has $10,000,000+ of death protection, the player is barred from buying life insurance for 90 days after execution/extension (or until the Team notifies him it has stopped pursuing coverage) so the Team can pursue its own policy.
conditions: Contract entered into or extended on or after the effective date
exceptions: Certain minimum-salary contracts signed after the first Regular Season day or lacking full first-Season protection are excluded from the reimbursement provision
thresholds: death protection cap $30,000,000; insurance reimbursement ceiling $85,000,000; 90-day insurance bar at $10,000,000+
